summary:
A square hall on a stone podium (x 8..143), ringed by 14 quartz columns a side on a 9-block rhythm in front of red terracotta walls, with a polished granite band and a gray eave beam. Over it sits a hand-profiled concave yellow hip roof (eave at y 24, flat top at y 41) with gray hip ridges and corners that flick up, lit by ochre froglight tiles set into the roof.
On the south front the eave lifts into a tall gray portal: two upswept fins rising to y 47, six tall columns and a lit glass lobby behind them, reached by broad accessible slab steps. These are the building's signature features. Square hall on a raised stone podium: 52 quartz columns, red walls with a granite band, a great yellow concave-hip roof with corner upsweeps, gold tips, and froglight tiles.
The south portal has a raised eave between two upswept stone fins, six tall columns, a lit glass lobby and a "SUN YAT-SEN" board.
Floodlit at dusk by shroomlight wells, gallery lanterns, chandeliers and lamp posts, with hedged lawns around the podium.

podium, steps, colonnade, walls: parts/shell.mjs builds the podium, the south steps with cheek walls, 46 short columns, the red walls with pilasters, the granite band and the eave beam ring with brackets. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt, and `mcd check` reports no floating blocks. The six portal columns, the south wall between the fins and the three door-bay openings are left for later parts.
polish: I did not render or look at the tiles, so the look of this part is unchecked.
I did not run `mcd fit`.
I did not tick the elements.md items; I only added a note to plan.md.
P3 must build the six tall portal columns (centres 53..98 on z 134). The beam ring over x 53..98 at z 133..135 has nothing under it until they exist, so it is unsupported until then.
The south red wall and its pilasters are left out for x 49..102 (portal and lobby glass). P3/P4 must fill that span.
P4 must build the door bays: x 73..78 on the north wall, and z 73..78 on the east and west walls. Those spans are air gaps in the red walls.
I added a smooth_stone block at y 20..21 on every short column to carry the beam; it is not in the plan.
Lamp posts, floodlight wells and gallery lanterns are left to P5.
`mcd check` reports 12 orphan blocks that I did not look into.

waste.tool: A beam_over_columns helper in the vocabulary, or an `eave_beam(ring)` that includes the capital-to-beam stack.

waste.cost: 4 calls, roughly 10 minutes of box-orientation checking.
waste.tool: A `wall_ring(hall, columns, gaps)` helper that makes all four runs from the hall rectangle.

companions.task: Add the column stack from y 19 up to the beam, the capital blocks, and a worked corner treatment where the pilasters meet the corners.
Set the lamp posts on the cheek walls and the podium corners, and the floodlight wells beside the columns.

summary:
great yellow roof: P2 great roof built in parts/roof.mjs: concave-hip shell with corner lift and terracotta courses (roof_shell, portal cut-out x 52..99 z 120..141 skipped), gray hip ridges on all four diagonals, and the top deck at y 41 with a y 42 rim and gold corners.
Corner flicks are placed with corner_flick and gold tips, each step on a solid stone wedge so it is supported. make.sh runs whole: roof 40,060 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check shows no floating blocks.
Renders read as a yellow hip roof with visible tile courses and corner tips; the flicks read as stepped stone, not a smooth sweep.
polish: Corner flicks are stepped sawtooth wedges, not a smooth curl; refine if the dusk glance wants a sweep.
No roof.json written: the plan asks for a direct generator, so runParts prints 'roof: skipped' (harmless).
The south cut-out x 52..99 z 120..141 is left empty for P3 (portal) to fill; the P1 eave brackets at z 134 show as orphans until P3 replaces the short columns.
plan.md has no checkbox list, so only elements.md's four roof items were ticked (not plan.md).

waste.what: Hand-wrote the top-deck rim loop (y 42 smooth_stone on the d=30 ring, gold at four corners) because roof_shell does not place it; roof_cell does it cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 1,300 cells looped by coordinate, one generator pass
waste.tool: a roof_rim(g, box, d=30, {gold corners}) vocab helper, or roof_shell placing the rim itself

waste.what: Hand-wrote the solid wedge under each corner_flick step so the curl is supported; corner_flick alone leaves stairs floating in air at y 28..30.
waste.cost: 16 wedge columns computed from the d-table, about 60 blocks placed by loop
waste.tool: corner_flick(g, corner, {support: true}) that fills down to the roof surface, or a hip_ridge/corner_flick pair that shares the surface function

waste.what: Did not know the return shape of hip_ridge and corner_flick (placed as an array in one, a count in the other), so the report line had to guess with fallbacks.
waste.cost: one retry of the log line, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: vocab helpers documenting {placed: number, refused: [...]} in one shape

waste.what: Checked the corner upsweep and tip by eye from the zoom and front-left tiles rather than against a measured profile.
waste.cost: 3 renders
waste.tool: mcd render --closeups on the roof corner plus a roof-profile printout of the top per ring

companions.task: Cut the corner flick as a true curl: stone stairs stepping up to the gold tip with a smooth profile, instead of the stepped wedge.
Confirm the tile course rhythm (terracotta every third ring) and the eave lift at the corners once the portal part is in, from the south-east view.

summary:
south portal: P3 south portal built in parts/portal.mjs: fins x2 (x 49..51 / 100..102, to y 45, stone_stairs flicks, gold tips at y 47), six tall quartz columns on z 134 (y 3..36), portal_lintel x 49..102 z 130..141 with dentils, deck and parapet, and the mid beam y 30..31.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the portal line shows 0 REFUSED in parts-report.json and no off-palette blocks; mcd check shows no floating or unsupported blocks.
Ticked elements.md (fins, tall columns); plan.md Notes lists the P1 conflict and the removed fin shroomlight.
polish: P1 conflict: shell.mjs's eave beam ring (y 22..23, z 133..135 across all x) and its z 134 brackets (y 21) run through the six tall portal columns. About 108 column cells at y 22..23 and 12 at y 21 were refused and stay as P1's smooth_stone collar. Fix in shell.mjs: skip the beam fill and brackets for x 52..99 on z 134.

Roof cut-out is P2's job: roof_shell must skip x 52..99 z 120..141. The lintel covers only z 130..141, so over the lobby (z 120..129) there is no deck at y 37..41. Either P2 or the plan should close that strip.
Fin-tip floodlight: the shroomlight under each flick was removed because it had nothing to hang on. P5 needs another way to light the gold tips at y 47.

Lintel: 395 cells refused, all inside the fin footprints (x 49..51 / 100..102, y 37..41), which is the intended overlap. Dentils at y 36 along z 141 show as orphans in mcd check; they hang under the lintel by design.

waste.what: Probed individual cells to check whether the portal columns, lintel and beam were actually placed, by writing a throwaway script that calls blockAt on a list of coordinates.
waste.cost: 2 probe runs, about 13 coordinates
waste.tool: A `mcd probe build.nbt x,y,z ...` command (or a `--cells` option on mcd check) that prints the block at each cell and its layer-by-layer neighbourhood.

waste.what: Found out by reading the helper source that column() and portal_lintel() refuse occupied cells silently. The refusal counts never reached parts-report.json, which said 'refused 0' while about 120 column cells were skipped.
waste.cost: 1 read of vocab/h3.mjs and h1.mjs, 1 rebuild
waste.tool: runParts should collect the refused lists that vocab helpers return (column, portal_lintel, fin) into the part's report, not only writes made through the guard.

waste.what: Removed the fin's orphan shroomlight after the check flagged it, by hand, and noted the P1 beam-ring clash in plan.md by hand.
waste.cost: 3 check/rebuild cycles
waste.tool: `mcd check --contract` for the cross-part conflicts: a check that compares each part's cells against the earlier parts' cells would have shown the P1 clash before writing the portal.

waste.what: Hit a BSD sed -i error (macOS needs an explicit backup suffix), so the elements.md tick was redone with Edit.
waste.cost: 1 failed command
waste.tool: A tick command, e.g. `mcd tick elements.md 'Upswept fins'`, that edits the checklist without shell quoting.

companions.task: Build the two stone_stairs flicks at z 142..143 y 46 and check the facing and half of each stair against the fin's upswept line.
Set the gold_block tips at (x0+1, 47, 143) and the top-deck corners, and check they sit flush with the tip line of each fin.
Light the fin tips and the portal lintel underside, since I removed the shroomlight that was meant to do it.
Fit the lobby glass wall behind the portal columns (P4), with the mullion grid lined up to the column centres at x 53..98.

summary:
glazing and signs: P4 glazing and signs built in parts/facade.mjs: south lobby glass wall (x 55..96, y 3..36, z 130) with mullions, transoms and four open door pairs; lit E/W/N door bays on span 73..78.
SUN YAT-SEN name board (black_concrete, gold frame, yellow_wall_banner letters) at x 64..87, y 32..35, z 133. make.sh whole, no refusals or off-palette blocks, fit OK.
Open conflict: the P3 tall columns at x 70..72 and 79..81 (z 133..135) occupy the board and letter cells, so the name is not whole in the merged build until P3 or the plan moves.
polish: Name board and letters collide with the P3 tall portal columns (x 70..72, 79..81, z 133..135, y 3..36): in the merged build those cells are refused, so the board has gaps and the letters break. Fix belongs in the plan (P3 columns or board span); noted in plan.md Notes.
Letters are yellow_wall_banner (yellow cloth with black letters) rather than gold letters on black: a black base would be off-palette. Palette-valid, but reads as the inverse of the plan's wording.
The P1 polished_granite band runs across the lobby glass at y 20..21, a frieze bar through the glazing; kept as built, not a refusal.
Elements item 'Mid beam + name board' left unticked: the name board is built but the beam at z 131..132 y 30..31 is P3's and the column clash is open.
Not checked in the merged build: P3 is a stub in this copy, so the board's support and the portal column cells were not tested against the real portal.

waste.what: Worked out the glass wall, door bay and board coordinates by hand from plan.md and the helper sources, then ran a separate probe to see which cells the shell had already filled.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls of reading helper source and probing cells
waste.tool: A check that lists, per part, which of its planned cells are already taken by earlier parts (the refused list before the build, not after), and the plan's own collisions such as tall portal columns through the name board.

waste.what: Found by trial that plaque()'s banner letters take their base dye from the board colour, so a black board gives black_wall_banner, which is off-palette. Switched to bannerWord with base yellow by hand.
waste.cost: 2 rebuilds and a palette check
waste.tool: A plaque/bannerWord option that picks the banner base from the palette (for example base: 'yellow' with a palette check), or a palette-aware default in name_board.

waste.what: Confirmed the glass wall and door bays by zoom and cell probes one at a time, not by one front render.
waste.cost: 4 zoom calls and a probe script
waste.tool: mcd elevation of one face with the part's cells highlighted, so a glazing check is one image.

companions.task: Settle the name board's footing with the portal crew: the tall columns at x 70..72 and 79..81 cut through the board and its letters, so one of them has to give way before the sign reads.
Lay the SUN YAT-SEN letters in gold banner lettering on the black board, one line per panel between the portal columns, and check each letter stays clear of the columns.

summary:
dusk lighting: P5 dusk lighting built in parts/lights.mjs: 3 lobby chandeliers on a new y 37 lobby lid, 56 floodlight shroomlights on the deck at y 3, gallery lanterns on all four lines (south skipped in the portal span), lamp posts on the cheeks and podium corners, and shroomlights under the fin tips. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; lights reports 586 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
Roof lights are NOT built: roof_light() writes into the roof's tiles, which runParts locks (verified with a 2-part test), so the roof part must place the ochre_froglight grid and ridge feet.
polish: Roof lights not placed by this part: runParts refuses roof_light() writes into the roof part's tiles (verified). The roof part (P2) must lay ochre_froglight at x,z = 14+8k (k 0..15), skipping x 52..99 z 120..141 (portal), plus ridge feet (38,38), (113,38), (38,113), (113,113). Roof-top and roof dusk light is unverified until then.
Flood wells stand at y 3 on the deck, not flush at y 2: the shell owns the deck cells, so flood_well(o.over) would be a locked write. Decide with P1 whether the deck well cells should be left as air.

Lobby lid (smooth_stone, x 55..96 z 122..129, y 37) is my addition, not in plan.md. It is the chain anchor for the three chandeliers. It floats until P3 builds the portal lintel at z 130. Portal or plan owner should confirm the lid, or give the chandeliers another anchor.
Fin-tip shroomlights at (50,45,142) and (101,45,142) float until P3 builds the fins (portal was a stub in this copy). They touch the fin top at z 141 once built.
Shell (P1) leaves 8 orphan slabs at y 21 z 134 (eave brackets dangling on the south line): flagged for the shell owner, not lights.

Dusk light was measured only on the deck (y 3): the outer deck and gallery read lit (mostly 6-F). The hall interior is dark but unbuilt. Lobby and roof were not measured (no rooms.json rooms; roof absent).

waste.what: Perimeter column centres, outboard well cells and gallery midpoints were worked out by hand from COLUMN_CENTRES (loops in lights.mjs).
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of coordinate reasoning and 2 rebuilds
waste.tool: A vocab helper such as perimeterColumns(side) and galleryLanterns(side) (or flood_well(side) / gallery_lantern_line(side)) would put this in one call.

waste.what: Discovered that roof_light() is refused by the lock only by running it. Its refusal shows up as a silent 0 placed, not a REFUSED line, because the helper returns blocked without writing.
waste.cost: one throwaway 2-part runParts test script and one wrong-cell retry
waste.tool: runParts should report helper-level blocked cells per part (not only g.set refusals), and a dry-run flag that lists cells an earlier part owns would have shown this before the build.

waste.what: Checked where the deck and lobby lid float by reading the full check output and the light map; the light map prints 200+ rows per level when there are no rooms.
waste.cost: about 3 reads of large output
waste.tool: mcd light --summary, or a per-part light and float summary in parts-report.json.

waste.what: flood_well() default refuses the deck cell with no message, so the wells first came out as 0 placed.
waste.cost: one rebuild
waste.tool: A helper that names the blocking cell and block in its return value (it already has blocked[]; print it in the part line).

companions.task: Lay the ochre_froglight tile grid and the four ridge-foot lights inside the roof pass (P2), where the roof tiles are placed, since the lights part cannot write into them.
Agree the lobby lid at y 37 with the portal worker, or choose another anchor for the three chandelier chains, and check it reads right from the south above the raised eave.

summary:
grounds: P6 grounds built in parts/grounds.mjs: dirt_path walks around the podium and up the south steps, coarse_dirt scrapes in the lawn, azalea hedge band z 144..147 (gaps at the flagpoles), 24 spruce topiary cones every 18 on the lawn strips, and 4 red-banner flagpoles in the south hedge.
Ground writes only where the y0 cell is still park grass on the # footprint; no REFUSED writes, no OFF-PALETTE blocks after the flagpole fix. make.sh saved a whole build.nbt; fit OK; check shows the grounds walkable with no grounds-caused orphans.
Two items in elements.md ticked (flagpoles, park); plan.md Notes records the flagpole substitution and the walk layout.
polish: Shell (P1, not this part) leaves 12 orphan smooth_stone_slab brackets at y 21 on z 134 (x 52..81), which dangle under the eave beam where the portal columns will stand; P3 or P1 should own them.
Grounds carry no light: the lawn, hedges and walks need P5's lanterns/shroomlights to reach light >= 1 at dusk (checked only by eye, `$MCD light` not run).
No render check of the dusk lawn at the Elephant Mountain view yet; only the look sheet at front n was rendered.

waste.what: Ground patches and walk edging were written as per-rectangle loops that test each cell for grass and onFootprint by hand (ground() helper I wrote in grounds.mjs).
waste.cost: about 4 rectangle calls, 2 tries, roughly 1400 dirt_path and 60 coarse_dirt cells checked one by one
waste.tool: a build-library `patch(g, box, block, { over: 'grass_block', footprint: true })` helper that paints ground blocks only on footprint cells that still hold a given block would have made this one line per patch.

waste.what: Hedge segments split by hand around flagpole gaps, and cone centres listed by hand every 18 along three lawn strips.
waste.cost: about 15 coordinate sets worked out by hand, one retry for the hedge gap at x 20/46/112/134
waste.tool: `hedge_run` taking a list of gaps, and a `topiary_row(g, {from, to, step, side})` helper that places cones along a strip would remove the hand arithmetic.

waste.what: flagpole() in vocab/h2.mjs places a red wall banner, which is off-palette in palette.json; I had to write a local pole with a standing red_banner and re-run make.sh.
waste.cost: one failed make.sh run and one retry
waste.tool: vocab `flagpole()` should take a `banner: 'standing'` option or use red_banner from palette.json, and make.sh/runParts could flag off-palette blocks before the build finishes.

waste.what: Checking the render by eye: I read the look sheet to confirm the hedge band, cones and walks at the scale of the whole plot, since no zoomed view was run.
waste.cost: one render and one image read
waste.tool: `mcd zoom build.nbt --at 20,1,145` on the flagpole gap would have confirmed the pole and hedge at a readable scale.

companions.task: Lay out the lawn patches, the coarse-dirt scrapes and the walk widths around the podium so the ground reads as worn park rather than a flat grass slab.
Trim and shape the spruce topiary cones and check their height and width against the podium edge and the lawn strips.
Light the hedge band and the walks to level 1 or more at dusk, so no lawn cell spawns mobs, and the flagpoles and cones show from the Elephant Mountain trail.
